'''Coleman Kcaj''' was an [[Ongree]] [[Gender|male]] [[Jedi Master]] who served the [[Jedi Order]] during the [[Republic Era|last]] [[Standard year|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]. During the [[Clone Wars]], Kcaj gained a seat on the [[Jedi High Council]] and then survived for years during the [[Great Jedi Purge]].

==Biography==
===Clone Wars===
Coleman Kcaj was an [[Ongree]] [[Gender|male]] [[Jedi Master]] [[Reproduction|born]] on [[Skustell]]<ref name="Join the Battle" /> who took a seat on the [[Jedi High Council|Jedi Council]], the governing body of the [[Jedi Order]]<ref name="The Wrong Jedi">{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}}</ref>, following the [[Skirmish on Florrum|killing]] of [[Adi Gallia]] on [[Florrum]] in [[19 BBY]].<ref name="19 BBY">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of "[[The Wrong Jedi]]," which includes Kcaj's first [[Time|chronological]] appearance, to [[19 BBY]].</ref>

Kcaj was present during a [[Jedi Council|Council]] meeting concerning the fate of [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]], who was accused of the [[Death|murder]] of [[Letta Turmond]] and orchestrating the [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar|bombing]] of the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]]. [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] said that the [[Galactic Senate]] wished to put her in a [[Republic Military|military]] trial. The Council expelled Tano from the Order after a debate and she was put on [[Trial of Ahsoka Tano|trial]] by the [[Galactic Republic]], but Padawan [[Barriss Offee]] was ultimately [[Duel at the Jedi Temple|revealed]] to be the true culprit.<ref name="The Wrong Jedi" />

[[File:JediCouncil-Conspiracy.png|thumb|left|250px|Coleman Kcaj (leftmost) participates in a Council meeting.]]
After [[clone trooper]] [[Tup]], whose malfunctioning and secret [[Behavioral modification biochip|biochip]] caused him to [[Battle of Ringo Vinda|murder]] [[Jedi]] Master [[Tiplar]], was sent to [[Kamino]] to have the incident investigated, Kcaj was present in a council meeting through [[Hologram|holographic form]] when Jedi Master [[Shaak Ti]] turned to the council with the belief that Tup may have a [[tumor]].<ref name="Conspiracy">{{TCW|Conspiracy}}</ref>

Later, Kcaj was present when the Council agreed to send Jedi Master [[Mace Windu]] alongside [[Junior Representative]] [[Jar Jar Binks]] on an [[Diplomatic mission to Bardotta|assignment]] to investigate a number of disappearances on [[Bardotta]], including that of their [[Queen]] [[Julia]].<ref name="The Disappeared 1">{{TCW|The Disappeared, Part I}}</ref> Kcaj was present when [[Plo Koon]] reported that he found the [[Sifo-Dyas's lightsaber|lightsaber]] of Master [[Sifo-Dyas]]. [[Yoda]] confirmed that it was and decided to investigate. Kcaj was again present when it was reported that [[Dooku]] was responsible for the creation of the [[Grand Army of the Republic|clone army]]. The Council decided to keep it a secret since people would lose trust in the Republic if the truth became publicly known .<ref name="Lost One">{{TCW|The Lost One}}</ref> Kcaj was later present when Yoda told the Council that he had heard the [[Force spirit|voice]] of long-dead Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] in his head, and hoped to learn the meaning of the communications from beyond. The Council all [[Meditation|meditated]] with Yoda, but nobody heard the voice.<ref name="Voices">{{TCW|Voices}}</ref>

Kcaj was later present when [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker]] discussed a giant [[kyber crystal]] they had [[Mission to Utapau|found]] on [[Utapau]]. Kcaj was present again when they reported that the [[crystal]] had been destroyed, causing Yoda to remind the Council of stories where kyber crystals were used for [[Superweapon|weapons]] by the [[Sith]].<ref name="The Big Bang">{{TCW|The Big Bang}}</ref>

[[File:Yoda7JediCouncil.png|thumb|250px|Kcaj and the Jedi Council discussed Yoda's report on Operation: Titan.]]
Later that year,<ref name="Yoda Date">The third arc of ''[[Star Wars: Yoda]]'' features [[Agen Kolar]] on the [[Jedi High Council]]. "[[A Seat on the Council]]" establishes that Kolar replaced [[Eeth Koth]], who served on the Council during [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|''The Clone Wars'': The Lost Missions]]. ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of "[[The Wrong Jedi]]" to [[19 BBY]]. ''Galactic Atlas'' also dates the beginning of [[Great Jedi Purge]], which includes the events of "[[Victory and Death]]," to 19 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. {{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-chronological-episodeorder|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Chronological Episode Order}} places ''The Lost Missions'' between "The Wrong Jedi" and "Victory and Death", dating the events of ''The Lost Missions'' to 19 BBY. Kolar was later seen on the Council during {{Film|III}}, the events of which ''Galactic Atlas'' also dates to 19 BBY, including the [[Operation: Knightfall|destruction]] of the [[Jedi Order]], limiting Kolar's tenure, and ''[[Star Wars: Yoda: Size Matters Not]]'', to that year.</ref> Kcaj was present at a meeting during which the Council heard Yoda's report of a devastating weapon known as [[Operation: Titan]] that would turn the tide of war in favor of the Confederacy. However, the available information on the enemy project was insufficient and Obi-Wan Kenobi mentioned that [[Anakin Skywalker]]'s forces had recently captured a [[Munificent-class star frigate|Separatist frigate]], suggesting that they sweep the vessel's databanks. Yoda agreed, deciding to go join Skywalker himself. Yoda and Skywalker followed their leads and learned that Operation: Titan involved the construction of a new droid army containing "[[megadroid]]s."<ref name="Yoda 7">[[Yoda 7|''Yoda'' 7]]</ref> The two later reported to the Council that the megadroids were under construction on the planet [[Golatha]], and informed them that they planned to destroy the [[Golatha factory|factory]] there before the megadroids could be deployed on the battlefield,<ref name="Yoda 8">[[Yoda 8|''Yoda'' 8]]</ref> a task that they were ultimately successful in completing.<ref name="Yoda 9">[[Yoda 9|''Yoda'' 9]]</ref>

Shortly after the [[Battle of Coruscant]], Kcaj attended a performance of [[Squid Lake]] at the [[Galaxies Opera House]] and was seen talking to [[Senator]] [[Sweitt Concorkill]] shortly before the show.<ref name="ROTS" />

[[File:ColemanKcaj.png|thumb|left|250px|Kcaj attending one of the Council's last meetings.]]
Near the end of the war, Kcaj was present when the Council granted Skywalker a seat on the Jedi Council, after he had been appointed there by [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]]. He was later present when the council discussed about how Palpatine had said that [[General]] [[Grievous]] was hiding on Utapau and recommended they send Skywalker to lead the [[Battle of Utapau|campaign]]. However, the council decided that they needed a Master, with more experience, and decided on sending Kenobi instead. Shortly thereafter, Palpatine [[Proclamation of the New Order|declared]] himself [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] and Skywalker, having become the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Vader, helped [[Great Jedi Purge|destroy]] the Jedi Order.<ref name="ROTS" />

===The Jedi Purge===
{{Quote|This is a list of the surviving Jedi. Others may remain, but of these we are certain. Unfortunately… they have hidden themselves ''extremely well''.|[[The Grand Inquisitor]]|<ref name="Dark Lord 19">[[Darth Vader (2017) 19|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 19]]</ref>}}
During the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Kcaj was among the few Jedi to escape the ensuing carnage that was [[Order 66]].<ref name="Dark Lord 19" /> At one point presumed to have been killed,<ref name="VE">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Kcaj's name was later included on a holographic list compiled by the [[Inquisitorius]] of confirmed survivors in the [[time]] after the [[hunt for Eeth Koth]], having hidden from the Empire extremely well in the last five years.<ref name="Dark Lord 19" />

==Personality and traits==
Coleman Kcaj was an Ongree male, with [[Color|yellow]] [[eye]]s and yellow skin.<ref name="ROTS" /> He was 2.04 [[meter]]s, or 6 [[Foot|feet]], 8 inches tall.<ref name="Join the Battle" /> Kcaj was a valued member of the Jedi Council.<ref name="Pocket">''[[Star Wars Jedi Pocket Expert]]''</ref> During his younger years, he was a formidable warrior but over time he came to see battle as a tragic failure to find mutual understanding.<ref name="Join the Battle" />

==Powers and abilities==
Coleman Kcaj was well versed in [[Force-sensitive|Force sensitivity]], [[meditation]], [[lightsaber combat]], military strategy, and [[Diplomat|diplomacy]],<ref name="Join the Battle" /> the lattermost of which was a common trait among the negotiable Ongree.<ref name="Alien Archive">''[[Star Wars: Alien Archive]]''</ref>

==Equipment==
Coleman Kcaj wore [[Jedi apparel|Jedi robes]]<ref name="ROTS" /> and wielded a [[Coleman Kcaj's lightsaber|green single-bladed lightsaber]].<ref name="Super Graphic">''[[Star Wars Super Graphic: A Visual Guide to a Galaxy Far, Far Away]]''</ref>

During a performance of the opera Squid Lake at the Galaxies Opera House, Kcaj wore red-and-white patterned robes very similar to those worn by [[Junior Representative]] [[Jar Jar Binks]].<ref name="ROTS" />

==Behind the scenes==
Coleman Kcaj first appeared in the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars:'' Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']].<ref name="ROTS" /> He is completely computer-animated. Originally, Kcaj was called [[Sweitt Concorkill]], but the name was ultimately given to a [[Vurk]] [[Senator]] later on.<ref name="Insider 100">{{InsiderCite|100|Ask Lobot|Q&A}}</ref> There was originally some confusion between the Ongree Jedi [[Pablo-Jill]] seen in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] and the Ongree member of the Jedi Council seen in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], with early Set Diaries naming the latter Ongree Pablo-Jill and later Sweitt Concorkill, though he was eventually named Coleman Kcaj. The character was originally meant to be Pablo-Jill, but because the Ongree in Episode III needed a more detailed CGI model, a new character was created.<ref name="Hyperspace-Mocking Heads">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/postnotes/news20040227.html|series=Episode III Post Notes|text=Mocking Heads}}</ref><ref name="Hyperspace-Jedi Council Musical Chairs">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/postnotes/news20031125.html|series=Episode III Post Notes|text=Jedi Council Musical Chairs}}</ref><ref name="Hyperspace-Episode III Set Diary - The Jedi Council Puzzle">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/episode-iii/bts/setdiary/news20040828.html|series=Episode III Set Diary|text=The Jedi Council Puzzle}}</ref> The name Coleman Kcaj is in reference to [[Rob Coleman]]'s son Jack, with Kcaj being the reversed spelling of Jack.<ref name="Tweet">{{Twitter|ArfKeldo|status/1532948984414601216|[[Rob Coleman]]|date=2022-06-03|quote=Coleman Kcaj, who was named after my son, Jack 😄|archivedate=20220604045733}}</ref>

Initially upon the release of [[Part IV]] of ''[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'', on [[StarWars.com]] the corpse of Pablo-Jill was mistakenly named Coleman Kcaj.<ref name="Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/obi-wan-kenobi/part-iv-guide|text=Part IV Episode Guide | Obi-Wan Kenobi}}</ref> Nevertheless, in the concept art done by [[Kouji Tajima]], the art for this character was instead labeled as Pablo-Jill.<ref name="ArtStation">{{ArtStation|username=koujitajima|url=artwork/NGPvWz|name=[[Kouji Tajima]]|text=Pablo Jill - Obi Wan Kenobi}}</ref> [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] pointed out the Ongree in ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' doesn't have spots, closer resembling Pablo-Jill,<ref name="Spots">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1727031570991903218|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Coleman has spots. Pablo-Jill doesn't. I assumed it was PJ based on that (I think the asset is just called triangle-head).|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/CWmlZ}}</ref> but recommended that [[Wookieepedia]] give priority to StarWars.com than the concept art.<ref name="Wookieepedia">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1727049589969260995|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=I'd recommend they follow starwars-com's lead rather than take my assumptions to heart.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/aa2Uy}}</ref> StarWars.com later corrected its mistake and changed Coleman Kcaj's name to Pablo-Jill in the image description, but nevertheless, the article continued to incorrectly state that Pablo-Jill was a member of the [[Jedi Council]] seen in ''Revenge of the Sith''.<ref name="Episode Guide" />
